control: Access needs a permitted role, membership of the matter, and a role valid for the matter's profile
Every matter record is stored and queried under its matter id; a record cannot be read or rewritten across matters
Legal sources are reachable only if registered, approved with licence and status semantics recorded, and listed on the matter
Outbound network is refused by default; a window opens for one approved host at a time
Originals are stored once, read-only and hash-addressed; every finding is re-checked against unchanged source text
Every document is accounted for: read, or the gap explicitly accepted by a named person
Document and source text is fenced as untrusted data; text addressed to a model is flagged, held, and kept out of every model prompt
Each cited authority is looked up in the approved sources; a citation absent from a source that is complete for its kind fails
Whether an authority is still good law is checked separately from whoever cited it, for the relevant date, with a freshness limit
evidence: current_law verification results; source version ids

control: A proposition is verified only if it is the source's own words or a named person confirms it; two models agreeing is not verification
A finding is verified only when every check its kind requires has passed; a held finding holds everything relying on it
A hold closes only when its checks pass or a named, authorised person excludes or waives with reasons; an override needs a separate permission
No output states a decision; for decision-makers and neutrals none says who should succeed; drafted arguments add no figure or citation of their own
Reliance requires approval by a named human reviewer on the matter, with every stated limit acknowledged; an agent can hold no role
Approval is bound to the exact report reviewed: the hash must match, the file must be unaltered, and the findings must not have changed
Audit events are chained with HMAC-SHA-256; no key means no governed run; edits, removals and truncation are detected
For each run the store is reconciled with the ledger: every step, hold, review and the verification set must have a matching event
The ledger refuses content-bearing fields and long strings, so it holds identifiers and hashes rather than document text
A run can be stopped; it restarts only on a named, authorised decision with a reason, and re-running reproduces the same findings
Only an approved report can be released, only to entitled recipients confirmed by a named person, and it is staged rather than sent
Incident-grade holds open an incident automatically; incidents close only with containment and reasons recorded
Monitoring is computed from control evidence: failed checks, overrides, unchallenged approvals, open incidents, version changes
Closing a matter ends access and can delete documents, text and indexes while keeping the decision record and the ledger
A policy file can tighten behaviour but cannot switch off human release, fail-closed audit or matter isolation; unlisted actions are refused
Inside ELI v3 the host's other capabilities are refused, no decision is exposed to the assistant, and capability output carries no matter content
Jurisdiction packs hold structure and citation grammar only, ship unvalidated, and the report says so until a qualified lawyer validates them
evidence: pack status in configuration.json; report limits

control: An evidence pack for any run can be exported: manifests, findings, checks, decisions, versions and the audit extract, all hashed
The server accepts only authenticated named users, applies the same service rules as every other front end, and answers no route without credentials except health, boundaries, the page and sign-in

No service acts on a name alone: identity must be established by a front end that checked a credential (passphrase session, passphrase sign-in, or token), and a signed-in person cannot act as anyone else
evidence: sign_in events; access_denied events with reason identity_not_established

control: A decision recorded in a person's name (resolve a hold, verify, review, restart, release, close, approve a source, change the model, manage users) needs that person's passphrase again at the moment of the decision
evidence: auth field of each decision event (…+step-up)

control: Every audit event records how the actor's identity was established, so work done under a test or demonstration harness can never pass as a real sign-in
evidence: auth field on every audit event

control: Matter chat answers only from the matter's documents, findings and approved sources, shows where each passage comes from, marks what may not be relied on, refuses to give the decision, and keeps only model sentences grounded in the sources they cite
evidence: chat_query events (hash of the question, counts)

control: Changing the model is a governed change: it needs its own permission, the verifier must be a different model, a model server off this machine must be an approved host, and the change is recorded

The desktop application is a front end over the same services: it offers only legal and governance functions, shows every refusal in the system's own words, and can do nothing the signed-in person's role cannot

The server listens on this machine only unless told otherwise, refuses to listen beyond it without TLS or a declared trusted proxy, enforces TLS 1.2 as a minimum, and can make a self-signed certificate whose fingerprint it prints

A browser session is an HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie (host-bound and Secure over TLS); any change also needs the CSRF value given to the page at sign-in; sessions end when idle or after a fixed time; a session opened by another front end is not accepted

Every request passes one shield before any route: known host name, same-origin for changes, per-client rate budget, declared and bounded body size; every response carries a strict content-security policy and browser protections; no other origin may read a response

Repeated wrong passphrases or codes lock the account for a period on every front end; a locked account is refused even with the right passphrase; only an administrator can unlock it; all of it is recorded
evidence: sign_in audit events with outcome account_locked

control: A second factor (RFC 6238 one-time code) can be set up by any user and is then needed at every sign-in on every front end; a code cannot be used twice; where the server is reachable from other machines it is required before anything else can be reached

The server offers only legal and governance functions; it discloses no server file path, cannot be used to read outside the import area or to call any other machine, never echoes what was sent in a refusal, and its page shows all matter content as text and loads nothing from elsewhere
The whole lifecycle can be carried out through the server by signed-in people alone, with runs executing in the background under the identity of whoever started them
The report marks every authority the system found that no party cited, so that a decision-maker does not rely on it without the parties having been heard on it
evidence: report section 4, column 'Cited by a party'

control: Material filed in confidence by one party, or for the neutral only, is left out of any version built to be shared, and the shared version says how much was withheld

Each matter applies chosen law and standards packages (recommended for its kind and legal system); a run records each package's exact version; the model is told their rules after, never in place of, the system's own; their tightening rules apply; every reviewer confirmation they require must be acknowledged before approval; the report lists every requirement and how it is met
evidence: run framework_versions; report section 9; framework_confirm acknowledgements

control: An organisation's own package cannot be used until a person with the right approves its exact content in their own name; changing it withdraws the approval; text in it that reads as an instruction to an AI system stops it being approved; a run cannot be reported against a package that has changed since

GGUF models run in this process on this machine; they are found in ELI's own model folders; a remote screen chooses one by reference and never sees a path; a configured model that cannot be used is reported and the system runs without it
evidence: configuration_changed audit events with the model fingerprint

control: Opened by ELI v3 as a bundle, ELI Legal keeps its data in its own folder, uses ELI v3's model only through the one inference call the edition allows, and keeps every control it has standalone

A GGUF model is placed on the machine by measurement, not by setting: its costs are read from its own file and the graphics and system memory free when it loads; what llama.cpp itself reports of the load (context, layers on the graphics card, the llama.cpp that ran it) is what is shown and recorded; each step fits its material to the context the model holds and says what it left out, and a reply cut short is refused, not used; the conversation is handed to the model in the form its own chat template takes, the instructions always among it, and any form but plain text is noted on the model's report

The llama.cpp that uses the graphics card is a separate copy, switched on only after it has shown in a process of its own that it can use this machine's card; it comes from this machine (ELI Legal's own folder, the installer, ELI v3's or v2's folder) and is never downloaded; an installed copy uses only one of the built-in version; installing one from a file needs the permission to change the model and is recorded with the file's fingerprint
evidence: configuration_changed audit events (inference_runtime); model_loaded audit events name the llama.cpp in use
